sections.body:
whatisayurveda.com is published by the **Kairali Ayurvedic Group**, a family-run organisation whose work in Ayurveda goes back to 1908. It is a free, non-commercial reference site. Nothing is sold here — there is no shop, no cart, and no consultation fee to read a page.

We built it because most of the clearest, best-ranked writing about Ayurveda online comes from institutions outside the tradition, while the practitioners who train in and practise it are largely absent from the conversation. This site is our attempt to explain Ayurveda from inside the tradition, in plain language, and to hold ourselves to the same evidence and disclosure standards a good medical library would.

If you want the plain-English overview of the subject itself, start with our pillar guide, [what is Ayurveda](/what-is-ayurveda). This page is about who stands behind it.

sections.h2: Who are the Kairali Ayurvedic Group?
sections.capsule: Kairali is a family-run Ayurvedic group whose work in the tradition dates to 1908, now led by K.V. Ramesh and Gita Ramesh. Its practice spans Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village, an NABH-accredited hospital in Palakkad, Kerala, a WHO-GMP-certified pharmacy, and Ayurvedic treatment centres across several countries.
sections.body:
Kairali is not a publisher that decided to write about Ayurveda. It is an Ayurvedic organisation that decided to publish. That distinction is the whole point of this site.

The group's work sits on three pillars:

| Arm | What it is | Why it matters for this site |
|---|---|---|
| **Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village** | An **NABH-accredited** Ayurvedic hospital in Palakkad, Kerala, where patients are seen and treated under physician supervision | Real clinical practice — the physicians who review our pages treat patients here |
| **Kairali Ayurvedic Products (KAPPL)** | A **WHO-GMP-certified** Ayurvedic pharmacy and manufacturer | First-hand knowledge of how classical formulations are actually made and quality-controlled |
| **Kairali treatment centres** | Ayurvedic centres operating across several countries | Day-to-day practice of the tradition at scale |

The modern group is led by **K.V. Ramesh** and **Gita Ramesh**, with Abilash K.R. as Executive Director. The two accreditations above — NABH for the hospital and WHO-GMP for the pharmacy — are independent, audited quality standards. They are why, when a page here discusses the well-known concern about heavy metals in some Ayurvedic products, we can answer it from inside a certified manufacturing operation rather than at a distance. We cover that concern squarely on [is Ayurveda scientific?](/is-ayurveda-scientific).

Kairali built a free, citable reference staffed by Ayurvedic physicians to explain the subject accurately and honestly, without selling anything on the page.
sections.body:
Three things make this site worth building:

- **A gap worth filling.** Search for "what is Ayurveda" and you mostly find large hospitals and health publishers. That is good work, but it is Ayurveda described from the outside. A practitioner group can add something they cannot: first-hand experience of the treatments, the pharmacy, and the classical texts.
- **A standard worth meeting.** Ayurveda is a health topic, which means it should be held to the highest bar for accuracy and honesty. We aim to meet that bar visibly — named authors, a named medical reviewer, dated reviews, and real citations on every health page.
- **An honest, non-selling voice.** Because this site sells nothing, we can afford to say plainly where the evidence is strong, where it is thin, and where a claim would cross a line we will not cross.

We would rather be trusted than be loud.

sections.capsule: Our promise is honesty over hype. We describe what the classical texts and modern studies actually say, name the limits of the evidence, and never claim that Ayurveda cures, treats, or prevents any named disease. Where evidence is thin, we say so plainly. Every health page carries citations and a medical review.
sections.body:
Our editorial promise, in five plain commitments:

1. **We do not claim cures.** You will not read here that a herb or therapy cures, treats, prevents, or gives permanent relief from any named disease. We describe how things are *traditionally used* in Ayurveda and what studies have *looked at*, always with the evidence in view.
2. **We name the limits of the evidence.** Dosha theory has not been validated by modern biology. Rigorous clinical trials of many Ayurvedic therapies are few. We say this on the page, not in a footnote.
3. **We separate education from selling.** The body of an article is claim-free and independent. Where it is genuinely relevant, a clearly marked box may note where a therapy is practised or where a formulation is made. That is a signpost, never a sales pitch.
4. **We cite real sources.** Health pages carry numbered citations to authoritative references such as the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health [1] and peer-reviewed literature.
5. **We correct mistakes in the open.** If we get something wrong, tell us, and we will fix it and note the change.

This is general education, not medical advice. Ayurveda is best understood as a complement to conventional care, never a replacement, and no page here substitutes for consulting a qualified physician.

sections.h2: How is our health content reviewed? (Editorial policy)
sections.capsule: Every health page follows a fixed pipeline: a named writer drafts it, an Ayurvedic physician — Dr. Deepu John, BAMS — medically reviews it before publication, and each page shows its author, reviewer, and review date. Pages are re-reviewed periodically to keep facts and evidence current. Corrections are welcomed and logged.
sections.body:
This is our editorial policy in full. It governs every page that carries health information.

**The review pipeline.** No health page is published until it has passed through these steps:

1. **Draft by a named writer.** Every page has a named author, shown on the page. We do not publish anonymous health content.
2. **Sourcing and claims check.** The draft is checked against authoritative references, and against our claims rules: no disease-cure language, honest evidence framing, traditional-use wording where appropriate.
3. **Medical review by an Ayurvedic physician.** The page is reviewed before publication by **Dr. Deepu John, BAMS**, chief physician at Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village. He checks that the Ayurvedic content is accurate to the tradition and that nothing overstates what is known. Therapeutic pages — such as those on panchakarma and individual herbs — do not go live without his sign-off.
4. **Publication with a visible byline.** The published page shows its author, its medical reviewer, and the date it was last reviewed.

**Re-review cadence.** Health knowledge and the evidence base move. We re-review health pages periodically so that facts, citations, and safety information stay current, and we update the review date when we do. A page that has not been looked at in a long time is a page we treat as due for review.

This pipeline mirrors the model used by leading medical health libraries, where every article is reviewed by a qualified clinician before publication and re-checked over time [2]. For Kairali it also satisfies an internal rule: clinical content requires a physician's sign-off. One process, two obligations.

**A note on two people named Deepu.** Our medical reviewer is **Dr. Deepu John**, a physician. He is not the same person as Deepu, a member of Kairali's web team. We keep the distinction clear because a medical byline must mean a medical reviewer.

**Corrections.** If you find an error, write to **info@kairali.com**. We read every message, correct genuine mistakes promptly, and note material changes on the page.

sections.h2: Who writes and reviews these pages?
sections.capsule: Health content is written by named contributors with Ayurvedic and editorial backgrounds and reviewed by Dr. Deepu John, BAMS, chief physician at Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village. Gita Ramesh, a long-standing author and educator on Ayurvedic cooking and daily practice, anchors the group's editorial voice. Every reviewer's credentials are shown.
sections.body:
**Dr. Deepu John, BAMS — Medical Reviewer.** Dr. Deepu John holds a Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery (BAMS), the recognised Indian degree qualification in Ayurveda, and is chief physician at Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village, the group's NABH-accredited hospital. He reviews the health content on this site for accuracy to the classical tradition and for responsible framing of what is and is not known. Therapeutic pages carry his sign-off.

**Gita Ramesh — Editorial voice.** Gita Ramesh is a long-standing author and educator within the Kairali group, known for her writing on Ayurvedic cooking and daily practice (dinacharya). She helps set the plainspoken, practitioner's-eye register you will find across the site.

**Named contributors.** Individual pages are drafted by named writers with backgrounds in Ayurveda and in health editing. Each page shows who wrote it and who reviewed it, so you always know whose judgement you are reading. Credentials are stated, not implied.

sections.h2: How can you contact or correct us?
sections.capsule: If you spot an error, or want to suggest a source, write to info@kairali.com. We read every message, correct genuine mistakes promptly, and note the change on the page. This site offers general education only; it is not medical advice, and it is not a substitute for consulting a qualified physician.
sections.body:
The best way to reach us about anything on this site — a factual correction, a better source, a question about our review process — is **info@kairali.com**.

A few things to keep in mind:

- **This is education, not medical advice.** Nothing here diagnoses a condition or prescribes a treatment. For anything concerning your own health, please consult a qualified physician.
- **Ayurveda is a complement, not a replacement.** We present it as something to be understood alongside conventional medicine, not instead of it.
- **We do not sell from these pages.** Where a page notes that a therapy is practised at Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village, or that a formulation is made at Kairali's WHO-GMP pharmacy, that is context, not a call to buy.

To carry on reading, return to the main guide, [what is Ayurveda](/what-is-ayurveda), or read [the history of Ayurveda](/history-of-ayurveda) and where the tradition comes from.

faqs.q: Is the health information on this site medically reviewed?
faqs.a: Yes. Every health page is written by a named author and medically reviewed by Dr. Deepu John, BAMS, chief physician at Kairali — The Ayurvedic Healing Village, before publication. Each page shows its author, reviewer, and review date, and pages are re-reviewed periodically.

faqs.q: Does whatisayurveda.com sell products or treatments?
faqs.a: No. The site is purely educational and sells nothing on the page. Where relevant, a clearly marked box may note where a therapy is practised or a formulation is made, but the article text carries no sales language or efficacy claims.
